title: Strategic capacity-slicing and initiative surge playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Create an operational playbook that lets Product, Eng, and GTM teams slice company-level capacity into bounded initiative ‘lanes’ and rapidly allocate surge capacity without destabilizing SLAs or key features. This reduces manual firefighting during quarter spikes and ensures company OKRs have hedged resource plans.

Why now: We saw multiple quarter-to-quarter skews where high-priority initiatives consumed unbudgeted Dedicated capacity, increasing host costs and causing latency regressions on low-latency routes. The playbook provides clear guardrails for reallocation, escalation, and runway math.

Scope: Cross-functional (PM, Eng, SRE, Finance, Solutions), covers:
- Definition of capacity slices (baseline, reserved, surge) and how they map to OKR importance tiers.
- Rules for pre-approved surge (fast-path) vs. discretionary surge (review board).
- Entropy budget: how to cap emergency interventions per initiative per month.
- Decision flow: who approves capacity shifts, fallback models, and automated rollback windows.
- Telemetry/alerts: dashboards and SLOs used to trigger playbook actions.
- Runbook templates (communication, runbook incident notes, costing reconciliation).

Deliverables:
1) Playbook doc with decision matrix and runbook templates (Confluence link).
2) Roadmap changes to the initiative intake form that capture capacity sensitivity and pre-approved surge amount.
3) Console dashboard widgets showing slice utilization and surge forecasts.
4) Small automation: a Slack-based surge request that prepopulates a review ticket and notifies reviewers.
5) Quarterly review rubric to re-balance slices and update hedges.

Acceptance criteria:
- Playbook doc reviewed and approved by PM, Eng lead, SRE, and Finance.
- Surge request flow implemented in Slack and tested end-to-end with a mock request.
- Dashboard shows baseline/reserved/surge utilization per initiative for past 30 days.
- At least two initiatives onboarded to a slice model in Q2 pilot.

Success metrics:
- < 10% of emergency surge requests escalate to Execs per quarter.
- 20% reduction in month-over-month unplanned Dedicated spend attributed to initiative spikes.
- No SLO violations traced to surge reallocations during pilot.

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Overly tight slices could slow high-urgency work; mitigate with fast-path approvals.
- Automation complexity vs. speed: start with minimal viable Slack flow.
- Cultural change: requires teams to estimate capacity-sensitivity upfront.
